functional_principles: Seal every cut edge and drilled hole after fabrication, where factory surface treatment is lost
Carry a fluorescent tracer so coverage shows under a 365 nm UV torch
Stay compatible with laminate and edge-band adhesives
technical_requirements: Preservative of a type permitted for wood in India; termiticides likely need registration under the Insecticides Act (verify with a regulatory consultant)
Tracer visible at 1 m with a 365 nm torch, invisible under normal light, no bleed through 1 mm laminate
No loss of adhesive bond strength versus untreated edges

material_options.material: Borate preservative (e.g. disodium octaborate) in water
material_options.pros: Low toxicity, cheap, widely used for wood
material_options.cons: Leaches in wet areas; weak for kitchens and bathrooms

material_options.material: Primer or bitumen edge sealer only
material_options.cons: No termite action; moisture control only

processes.notes: Needs a partner with wood-preservative experience

production_comparison.notes: contract formulator can fill and pack

technical:cpt_5af7828f45.prototype_dimensions: 250 ml tin with brush; 365 nm UV torch; enough for one 2.1 m wardrobe (estimate, to be measured)
technical:cpt_5af7828f45.tolerances: Not applicable. Acceptance target: at least 95% of cut edge length fluoresces in the UV check.

bom.note: could be lent, not sold, per contractor

construction_sequence: Carpenter cuts and drills all panels
Apply sealant to every cut edge and hole
Homeowner or designer checks edges with the UV torch and marks gaps
Touch up, then apply laminate and edge band
technical:cpt_5af7828f45.assembly: No assembly; applied on site before laminate.
safety_requirements: Safety data sheet and labels as required for the chosen chemistry
Do not shine the UV torch into eyes
Keep away from food preparation surfaces
failure_modes: Sealant does not penetrate dense edges
tests: UV coverage check on 20 treated offcuts
Adhesive pull test against untreated controls
Field exposure of treated and untreated edge samples at a termite-active site for 3-6 months, ideally with a wood research lab
technical:cpt_5af7828f45.low_cost_validation: Buy an off-the-shelf borate wood preservative and a fluorescent additive, treat 20 plywood offcuts, check UV visibility and adhesive bond, and run a 3-6 month side-by-side exposure test before any formulation work.

functional_principles: Break hidden contact between wall or floor and the furniture carcass
Make any termite mud tube cross visible metal so it can be seen early
Carry the unit's load and prevent tipping
technical_requirements: Hold a loaded 2.1 m wardrobe (estimate 150 kg, to be checked) with a safety factor of at least 3
Anti-tip restraint on every tall unit
Gap 25-40 mm, kept clear of trims and fillers
Galvanised or stainless parts for humid interiors
Floor feet with a metal shield lip so termites cannot climb hidden

material_options.pros: Cheap, strong, local fabricators can make it
material_options.cons: Zinc coating damaged at cut edges

production_comparison.notes: hacksaw, drill and vice for the first prototypes
laser or punch press at a job shop
local fabricators can bend and drill
levelling feet and anchors bought in

technical:cpt_a38a414885.prototype_dimensions: Wall bracket: 2 mm GI, 60 x 60 mm legs, 40 mm wide, 30 mm standoff. Floor foot: 40 mm diameter, 30 mm high, M10 leveller, 60 mm shield lip.
technical:cpt_a38a414885.tolerances: Hole positions +/-0.5 mm; bend angle +/-1 degree; standoff gap 30 +/-3 mm.

bom.item: adjustable floor foot with shield lip

construction_sequence: Set unit with a 30 mm wall gap
Fix wall brackets with anchors suited to the wall
technical:cpt_a38a414885.assembly: Carpenter fits on site with a printed guide; about 45 minutes per wardrobe (assumption).
safety_requirements: Anchor type matched to brick, block or AAC wall
Structural review for tall or overhead units
failure_modes: Anchors pull out of weak walls
Carpenter bridges the gap with trims or filler
Termites climb hidden inside feet if the shield lip is missing
technical:cpt_a38a414885.maintenance: Remove the plinth every 6 months and look for mud tubes on metal.
tests: Static load at 3x expected load for 24 hours
Anchor pull-out tests in brick and AAC
Observation in 2 homes with past termite activity for 6 months
technical:cpt_a38a414885.low_cost_validation: Have a local fabricator make 2 sets for about ₹3,000 (assumption), load test with sandbags, and install in 2 volunteer homes with a termite history.

functional_principles: Check materials on site before cutting starts
Record evidence the homeowner can see remotely
Stay independent of the supplier and carpenter
technical_requirements: Checklist: ISI mark, CM/L lookup in the BIS Care app, grade (MR/BWR/BWP), thickness by caliper, core-gap check on an offcut, moisture reading, batch photos
Inspector paid by the homeowner only

production_comparison.notes: partner with an existing inspection agency

construction_sequence: Homeowner books through designer or society
Re-inspects if a mismatch is found
safety_requirements: Site safety for inspectors (footwear, no work at height)
failure_modes: Delivery time unpredictable, wasting inspector time
A visual check cannot confirm chemical treatment
tests: Pilot 10 visits; record minutes per visit, travel cost, and how often a mismatch is found
technical:cpt_53d7f7d4b8.low_cost_validation: Founder runs the first 10 visits through 2 interior designers before hiring anyone.
